questions.question: An aircraft is in steady level flight with its body axis 4° above the horizontal. What are its flight-path angle γ and its angle of attack α?
questions.explanation: The pitch angle is θ = γ + α. Level flight means a horizontal flight path, so γ = 0 and α = θ = 4°. Taking the body axis as the flight path swaps the two angles; giving both 4° counts the pitch angle twice; splitting it in half has no basis in the geometry.

questions.section: What the pilot sets and what the design sets
questions.question: With the sign conventions of this page (nose up positive, elevator positive trailing edge down), an aircraft has a nose-down pitching moment with its elevator at zero. Which elevator angle trims it?
options: Negative, trailing edge up, which adds a nose-up moment
Positive, trailing edge down, which adds a nose-up moment
Positive, because the moment to cancel is negative
Zero, because the angle of attack alone sets the trim
questions.explanation: Trim needs a nose-up moment to cancel the nose-down one. A trailing-edge-up elevator pushes the tail down and the nose up, and with this convention that is a negative δe. A trailing-edge-down elevator makes a nose-down moment, not a nose-up one; the sign of δe follows from the moment the elevator must add, here nose up, not from the sign of the moment it cancels; and the elevator, not the angle of attack alone, is the control that sets the moment to zero.

questions.question: An aircraft weighs mg = 25,000 N and has the drag polar CD = 0.020 + 0.045 CL2. What is its minimum thrust required in steady level flight?
questions.explanation: TR,min = 2mg√(K CD,0) = 2 × 25,000 × √(0.045 × 0.020) = 50,000 × 0.030 = 1,500 N. 750 N drops the factor 2 and gives only the parasite part; 1,732 N is the thrust at the minimum-power point, where CL = √(3CD,0/K) and CD = 4CD,0; 1,125 N multiplies the weight by K instead of by 2√(K CD,0).

questions.question: An aircraft with a parabolic drag polar has a minimum-thrust speed of 100 m/s. What is its minimum-power speed at the same weight and altitude?
questions.explanation: VPR,min = 3−1/4 VTR,min = 0.7598 × 100 = 76.0 m/s. 100 m/s assumes the minimum power and the minimum thrust come at one speed; 131.6 m/s multiplies by 31/4 instead of dividing; 57.7 m/s divides by √3 instead of 31/4.

questions.question: On a plot of power required PR against airspeed V with both axes starting at zero, where do you read the minimum-thrust speed?
options: Where a line from the origin just touches the curve
At the lowest point of the power-required curve
Where the power-required curve is steepest
Where the curve meets the power-available line
questions.explanation: The slope of a line from the origin to a point of the curve is PR/V = TR, so the shallowest line that still touches the curve marks the minimum thrust. The lowest point is the minimum-power speed, the curve is steepest at high speed where the parasite power grows as V3, and the crossing with PA is the maximum speed.

questions.question: A twin-engine propeller aircraft has a shaft power P0 = 500 kW per engine at sea level, propeller efficiency η = 0.80, and mad = 1.0. What is its total power available at full throttle where ρ/ρ0 = 0.50?
questions.explanation: With n = 2 and δt = 1, PA = n η P0 (ρ/ρ0)mad = 2 × 0.80 × 500 × 0.50 = 400 kW. 200 kW counts one engine; 500 kW leaves out the propeller efficiency; 800 kW leaves out the density factor.

questions.section: Maximum speed and the speed range
questions.question: For a jet, the term under the inner root of the maximum-speed formula, TA2 − TR,min2, comes out negative. What does this mean?
options: The thrust available is below the minimum thrust required
The jet can fly level only at its minimum-thrust speed
Only the smaller root holds, at the low-speed crossing
The jet must be solved with the propeller iteration
questions.explanation: The term equals TA2 − TR,min2, so it is negative when the engines cannot give even the minimum thrust required: no level flight is possible. A zero term gives one speed, the minimum-thrust speed; with a negative term neither root exists; and the propeller iteration is for an aircraft rated in power.

questions.question: An aircraft climbs at constant weight to an altitude where the air density is one quarter of the sea-level value. How do its minimum thrust required TR,min and its minimum-thrust speed change?
options: TR,min stays the same and the speed doubles
TR,min falls to a quarter and the speed doubles
TR,min stays the same and the speed halves
questions.explanation: TR,min = mg/(L/D)max has no density in it, so it does not change. The minimum-thrust speed grows as √(ρ0/ρ) = √4 = 2. Doubling the thrust treats it like the power; a quarter of the thrust follows the density; halving the speed inverts the square root.
